questions.q: Why put imputing, scaling, and encoding inside a Pipeline that is passed to cross_validate?
options: Each fold learns its imputer, scaler, and encoder only from that fold's training rows, preventing leakage
It makes any model train faster
It removes the need for a test set
It allows categorical labels to be used as the target
questions.explain: Steps are fitted inside each fold, so information from the validation rows never influences the transformations.

questions.q: Class weights barely changed average precision and ROC AUC in this project. Why?
options: Class weights only work on trees
Those metrics depend on how customers are ranked, and reweighting mostly shifts probabilities and decisions rather than ranking
The dataset was balanced
Cross-validation ignores class weights
questions.explain: Threshold-free ranking metrics stay similar; what changed was the decision at 0.5 (39% of customers flagged instead of 0.4%).

questions.q: The plain logistic model's average predicted probability was 0.111, but the balanced model's was 0.448. Why did the lesson keep the plain model?
options: It has more trees
It trains slower, which is safer
Balanced models cannot be saved
Its probabilities are honest, which suits choosing a threshold from costs later
questions.explain: The plain model's mean probability matches the real cancel rate. Balanced weights inflate probabilities, so they no longer mean 'chance of cancelling'.

questions.q: Cross-validated average precision was 0.258 for logistic regression and 0.247 for the tuned forest, with fold spreads near 0.05. What is the fair conclusion?
options: The forest is clearly worse
Tuning failed completely
Logistic regression is at least as good, but the gap is small compared with the fold-to-fold noise
The test set should be used to break the tie
questions.explain: The error bars overlap, so the honest claim is that the simple model is competitive, not that it is far better. The test set is never used to choose.

questions.q: What does a positive standardized coefficient such as days_idle = 0.30 mean?
options: Each idle day lowers cancellation risk by 0.30
The feature is missing 30% of its values
The feature should be dropped
Higher idle time is associated with higher cancellation odds, per one standard deviation
questions.explain: Positive coefficients raise the log-odds of cancelling. Because numeric features were standardized, the effect is per one standard deviation.
